rationale: Three evaluated points: attempt-00 (128x64x64, stages=1, swizzle=0) at 234.82 us, attempt-01 (64x128x64, stages=1, swizzle=16) at 235.12 us, and attempt-02 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16) at 221.79 us, the new best. All compiled, passed numerical checks, and used exactly 32768 smem with 3 blocks/SM; simulated DRAM was identical at 16.78 MB in every case, so the serpentine swizzle/small-tile locality hypothesis shows no traffic benefit in the simulator. The clear improvement came from num_stages=2, not from swizzle or traffic reduction. Accordingly I raise the pipeline weight from 1.25 to 1.5 to push HiGHS toward larger block_K and stages>1 (the stage=1 and block_K=32 points are now sampled; stages=3 with block_K=64 remains unexplored), keep traffic low at 0.75 since DRAM did not differentiate, keep launches and footprint at 1 (footprint is saturated at the cap and matches the estimator), keep the hard 32768 portability cap, keep threads fixed at 128, and keep full tile/stage/swizzle domains since M=N=K=2048 is divisible by all and exclusion so far removes only three points. Swizzle stays [0,4,8,16] to keep probing it alongside deeper pipelines, but it is deprioritized by the traffic weight. Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binary execution is not validated, and GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. This remains exploratory, not a claim of global optimality.
